newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No crisis in IGC, Denmark's Ersboell says.
newsitem.headline: No crisis in IGC, Denmark's Ersboell says.

text.p: Danish chief negotiator Niels Ersboell has strongly rejected talk of a crisis in the inter-governmental conference, saying real negotiations were only now beginning.
However, Ersboell said this IGC was different and more difficult than the previous two, which resulted in the Single European Act and the Maastricht treaty.
He said those two had had "clearly defined and basically agreed objectives."

"This time it is more difficult because we have...to come up with convincing improvements of the treaty," he told reporters on Tuesday after the end of the latest two-day IGC session in Brussels. "We have to find answers to some very difficult questions."
"But we are only at the beginning of negotiations," he added.
There is growing concern in some EU circles that the IGC talks -- which began in March and are due to end in mid-1997 -- have become bogged down.
But Ersboell said he was unconcerned. "It (the IGC) is certainly not in a crisis, no, not at all."
He said the IGC had a long timetable and that many months remained. "Inevitably this means that the tempo is affected by the time we have available," he said.
Ersboell said delegates had spent a lot of time "defining and to a certain extent refining" the national views.
"So now we are in a position where we begin to negotiate," he said.
The timetable for negotiations looked very much like the one for those leading to the Maastricht treaty, Ersboell added.
